teams.heading: Fiji beat Italy 23-21 at Twickenham in Nations Championship 11th-place final
teams.body: Jake White's side closed their Nations Championship with the 23-21 win over Italy at Twickenham. It was their first victory from six matches in the campaign and leaves them 11th of 12. Isoa Nasilasila captained an XV built around Caleb Muntz at fly-half and Terio Tamani at scrum-half, with Iosefo Masi and Vinaya Habosi in midfield. Italy's captain for the day, Niccolò Cannone, had said beforehand that Fiji had changed a lot since the sides met in Udine.

teams.heading: Sam Warburton hails Borthwick's 'stroke of genius' in resting Maro Itoje
teams.body: Itoje skipped July's Southern Series, missing South Africa in Johannesburg, Fiji in Liverpool and Argentina in Santiago del Estero, on a break the former Lions captain says Borthwick proposed. Writing in The Times, Warburton pointed to last Saturday's 37-12 win over New Zealand, where Itoje made 49 ruck entries to Ollie Chessum's 31: "That is an absolutely monstrous effort." Against Japan the lock had the most tackles, 19, in 63 minutes. He captains the side again in today's third-place play-off rematch at Twickenham.

teams.heading: Galthié recalls Thomas Ramos and picks 6-2 bench for Springbok final
teams.body: Ramos is back at No. 15 for the final against South Africa, recovered from injury, with Théo Attissogbe moving to the wing in place of the injured Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang. Matthieu Jalibert partners Antoine Dupont at half-back and Anthony Jelonch replaces Grégory Alldritt in the back row. Galthié's bench splits 6-2, with Jean-Baptiste Gros recovered from a week-long doubt to join Peato Mauvaka and Régis Montagne. Planet Rugby reads the choice as a possible reply to Rassie Erasmus holding his strongest scrummaging front row in reserve.

teams.heading: Tadhg Beirne handed Ireland captaincy for Wallabies Test after Dan Sheehan suspension
teams.body: Beirne took the armband for Friday's fifth-place final against Australia, with Sheehan sitting out a two-game ban and Nick Timoney restored at No. 8 — one of two enforced changes from the side that beat South Africa 20-17. Beforehand, the stand-in skipper was frank about the year, conceding the summer tour was not as strong as Ireland wanted and that July's 33-31 win over the Wallabies in Sydney came "by the skin of our teeth."

teams.heading: Tommaso Menoncello needs shoulder surgery, putting his Italy Six Nations in doubt
teams.body: Italy's Nations Championship ended in a 23-21 defeat by Fiji, and Friday brought worse news: Toulouse said Menoncello requires surgery next week on a recurring shoulder injury, likely ruling him out for three to four months and leaving next year's tournament in doubt. The 24-year-old was hurt in training on Monday, the latest setback in an injury-blighted first season since joining the French champions as their sole recruit. Named 2024 Six Nations player of the tournament, he has been a cornerstone of Italy's upsurge under Gonzalo Quesada.

teams.heading: Rory Darge returns as captain in Townsend's 11 changes for Argentina
teams.body: Finn Russell is back at fly-half and Darge returns from injury to lead the side in Sunday's seventh-place final at Twickenham. Only Darcy Graham, Rory Hutchinson, Jamie Dobie and Jonny Gray survive from the Japan rout, with Hutchinson at 12 inside Huw Jones. With the squad's specialist eights injured, Magnus Bradbury starts at No. 8: "I'm sure he knows it's a big opportunity for him ahead of the Six Nations," said Townsend, who also weighed up hooker Seb Stephen there before ruling it out.

teams.heading: Dafydd Jenkins reclaims Wales armband for Japan, feeling 'a different person'
teams.body: Regular captain Dewi Lake and deputy Jac Morgan both drop to the bench for today's ninth-place play-off. That hands the Exeter lock the armband more than two years after Warren Gatland made him skipper for the 2024 Six Nations, when Wales lost every match. Jenkins wins his 35th cap and says he feels “a lot more settled now within the squad.” Ryan Elias starts at hooker in Lake's place. Tandy called the appointment “massive credit for him, so well-deserved and a great opportunity for him to lead the team.”

Up front, Joaquín Moro starts at openside with Facundo Isa dropping out and Juan Martín Scelzo moving to No. 8, while Rodrigo Martínez replaces the injured Boris Wenger at loosehead. Faustino Sánchez Valarolo comes in at inside centre, with Justo Piccardo dropping to the replacements.

teams.heading: Les Kiss stood by his 23, handing James Ramm a Wallabies debut
teams.body: James Ramm wore No. 11 at Twickenham, completing a back three with Tom Wright and Max Jorgensen, while Teddy Wilson was also in line for a first cap from the matchday squad. The 23 was the one named earlier in the week, with Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii and Len Ikitau paired in midfield and Carter Gordon and Kalani Thomas at half-back. It was also Kiss's first Test against Ireland as Wallabies coach, the side he once served as an assistant under Joe Schmidt.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones hands Taufa Latu first Test start in wholesale Japan changes
teams.body: Latu earned the nod for the ninth-place final against Wales after coming off the bench in last week's 5-67 defeat by Scotland. Michael Stolberg partners captain Warner Dearns in the second row and co-captain Naoto Saito starts at scrum-half, while Ryosuke Iwaihara and Seina Kimura were ruled out after that loss. The back row is unchanged, keeping Ben Gunter, the competition leader for dominant tackles (11) and jackals (six), at the breakdown where Japan poached Welsh ball six times when Wales won 28-21 in round four.

teams.heading: No All Blacks drug-tested after any of four Springbok series Tests
teams.body: The Times revealed that Rugby's Greatest Rivalry — the joint venture between New Zealand Rugby and SA Rugby, which the Springboks won 3-1 — passed without a single post-match test, three Tests in South Africa and one in Baltimore. Testing was delegated to the South African Institute for Drug-Free Sport, whose chief executive, Khalid Galant, said it was mandated only for out-of-competition work and was never asked to test during the South African leg. World Rugby says players remain in its year-round unannounced testing pool.

teams.heading: Manie Libbok backs Stormers bond with Feinberg-Mngomezulu for France final
teams.body: Libbok returns to the starting XV at fly-half for the Nations Championship final against France at Twickenham, with Feinberg-Mngomezulu moving to full-back to accommodate him. “We gel nicely because we’ve played a lot together, even back at the DHL Stormers,” said the 29-year-old. He came off the bench against Italy and France and missed the squad for last weekend's 20-17 defeat to Ireland, in which regular full-back Damian Willemse was injured and ruled out. Cobus Reinach partners him at scrum-half.
